name: Electrochemistry
tagline: Electron transfer, batteries, fuel cells, and electrodeposition.
seo_title: Electrochemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Electrochemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in batteries, fuel cells, electrolysis, corrosion and electrosynthesis.

definition.lead: Electrochemistry studies reactions that move electrons through a circuit: reactions that make electricity, and electricity that drives reactions.
definition.body: Batteries, fuel cells, electrolysers, corrosion, sensors and electroplating all run on redox reactions at electrodes. It sits at the centre of the energy transition, from lithium-ion batteries to green hydrogen.

timeline.title: Animal electricity
timeline.text: Luigi Galvani reports frog legs twitching when touched with two metals.
timeline.why: Started the debate that led to the battery.

timeline.title: The voltaic pile
timeline.text: Alessandro Volta stacks zinc and copper discs separated by brine-soaked cloth.
timeline.why: The first continuous source of electric current.

timeline.title: Sodium and potassium
timeline.text: Humphry Davy isolates sodium and potassium by electrolysis.
timeline.why: Electricity became a tool for discovering elements.

timeline.title: Faraday's laws
timeline.text: Michael Faraday relates the amount of chemical change to the charge passed, and names the electrode, anode and cathode.

timeline.title: The first fuel cell
timeline.text: William Grove combines hydrogen and oxygen to produce electricity.
timeline.why: The ancestor of today's fuel cells.

timeline.title: The lead–acid battery
timeline.text: Gaston Planté invents the first rechargeable battery.
timeline.why: Still used to start most cars.

timeline.title: Cheap aluminium
timeline.text: Charles Hall and Paul Héroult independently invent aluminium electrolysis.
timeline.why: Turned a precious metal into a common one.

timeline.title: The Nernst equation
timeline.text: Walther Nernst relates electrode potential to concentration.

timeline.title: Nobel Prize for lithium-ion
timeline.text: Awarded to John Goodenough, Stanley Whittingham and Akira Yoshino.
timeline.why: Recognized the battery behind the mobile and electric-car revolution.

quiz.q: What does a salt bridge do?

Supplies the electrons that flow in the wire
Stores energy so the cell can be recharged
Measures the voltage between the electrodes
quiz.explain: Without it, charge builds up and the current stops.

Painting it with a waterproof varnish

From the cathode to the anode
